lines.say: How does a submarine sink on purpose, and then come back up?
lines.caption: Submarine
lines.cap: How does a submarine sink on purpose, and then come back up?

lines.say: The trick is a set of big tanks in its hull, called ballast tanks.
lines.caption: Ballast tanks
lines.cap: The trick is a set of big tanks in its hull, called ballast tanks.

lines.say: Open the vents, and seawater floods in. Now the sub is heavier than the water around it, so it dives.
lines.caption: Flood
lines.cap: Open the vents, and seawater floods in. Now the sub is heavier than the water around it, so it dives.

lines.say: Small wings called hydroplanes steer it, and trim tanks keep it hovering at depth.
lines.caption: Hydroplanes
lines.cap: Small wings called hydroplanes steer it, and trim tanks keep it hovering at depth.

lines.say: To surface, compressed air blasts into the tanks and forces the water out.
lines.caption: Blow
lines.cap: To surface, compressed air blasts into the tanks and forces the water out.

lines.say: Lighter again, it shoots back up.
lines.caption: Surface
lines.cap: Lighter again, it shoots back up.
